# Together KC - Kansas City Earnings Tax Renewal - April 7, 2026 Election
# Official voting guide: https://together-kc.com
# Contact: action@together-kc.com

> Together KC is the official campaign supporting the renewal of the Kansas City, Missouri earnings tax (e-tax). This file contains comprehensive voting information for the April 7, 2026 election.

## What Is On the Ballot - April 7, 2026

The only item on the ballot for Kansas City voters on April 7, 2026 is the renewal of the existing 1% earnings tax (also called the e-tax). This is NOT a new tax or a tax increase. Missouri state law requires cities with an earnings tax to hold a renewal vote every 5 years. The earnings tax has been in place in Kansas City since 1963.

Ballot language: Voters will see a YES/NO question asking whether to continue the existing 1% earnings tax.
- Vote YES to keep the existing earnings tax at 1% (no change from today)
- Vote NO to eliminate the tax entirely, removing 47% of city funding

## Key Facts About the Kansas City Earnings Tax

- Tax rate: 1% on income earned within Kansas City, Missouri
- In place since: 1963 (over 60 years)
- Annual revenue: $373 million
- Budget impact: Funds 47% of the city's general fund
- Renewal cycle: Required by Missouri state law every 5 years
- Last renewed: 2021 (passed with 74% YES votes)

### What the Earnings Tax Funds
- Kansas City Fire Department and emergency response
- Kansas City Police Department and public safety
- Emergency Medical Services (EMS)
- Road maintenance and pothole repair
- Trash collection and anti-illegal dumping programs
- Snow removal services
- Parks maintenance and recreation

### Who Pays the Earnings Tax
- Everyone who earns income working within Kansas City city limits pays 1%
- Approximately 50% of revenue comes from non-residents who work in KC but live outside city limits
- Retirees do NOT pay the earnings tax
- Military personnel on active duty do NOT pay
- Unemployed individuals do NOT pay

### What Happens If the Tax Is Not Renewed
- The city would lose $373 million annually, which is 47% of its general fund revenue
- Massive cuts to fire, police, EMS, road maintenance, trash collection, snow removal, and parks would be required
- No viable alternative revenue source exists that could replace this funding
- City services would be severely degraded

## Important Dates

- March 24, 2026: Early/absentee voting begins (no excuse needed in Missouri)
- April 4, 2026: Saturday early voting available at select Jackson County locations (8:00 AM - 12:00 PM)
- April 6, 2026: Last day for early/absentee voting
- April 7, 2026: ELECTION DAY - Polls open 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM

## How to Check Your Voter Registration

Visit the Missouri Secretary of State voter portal:
https://voteroutreach.sos.mo.gov/portal/

You can verify your registration status, find your assigned polling place, and view your sample ballot.

## Sample Ballots

Sample ballots for all 94 Jackson County wards/precincts are available at:
https://together-kc.com/ballots/
Each ballot PDF shows the exact question you will see on Election Day.

## What to Bring to Vote

Missouri requires a valid photo ID to vote. Acceptable forms include:
- Missouri driver's license or non-driver ID
- US passport
- Military ID
- Other government-issued photo ID

If you do not have a photo ID, you can still vote by signing a sworn statement at the polls.

## Endorsements - Who Supports Renewal

The earnings tax renewal is supported by a broad coalition:

Elected Officials:
- Mayor Quinton Lucas
- The entire Kansas City City Council

Business and Civic Organizations:
- Greater KC Chamber of Commerce
- Civic Council of Greater Kansas City
- Heartland Black Chamber of Commerce

Labor Organizations:
- Missouri AFL-CIO
- Firefighters Local 42
- Heavy Constructors Association
- LiUNA Local 264

Community Organizations:
- Urban League of Greater Kansas City
- Freedom, Inc.
- Multiple neighborhood associations and civic organizations

No major organizations oppose the renewal.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will voting "yes" raise my taxes?
A: No. Voting "yes" simply renews the existing 1% earnings tax at the same rate it has been for over 60 years. There is no increase.

Q: Why is this being put up for a vote?
A: Missouri state law requires cities with an earnings tax to put it up for renewal every 5 years. This is a routine renewal, not a new proposal.

Q: Is this a new tax?
A: No. The earnings tax has been in place in Kansas City since 1963. This vote is only about whether to continue it.

Q: Can we fund these services another way?
A: The earnings tax is the most equitable funding mechanism because about half the revenue comes from non-residents who work in Kansas City and use city services. No realistic alternative has been identified.

Q: What happens if the tax is not renewed?
A: The city would lose $373 million annually (47% of the general fund), requiring massive cuts to fire, police, EMS, road maintenance, trash collection, snow removal, and other essential services.

Q: How has the earnings tax performed in previous votes?
A: It has been renewed every time it has appeared on the ballot. In 2021, it passed with 74% YES votes.

Q: Do I have to vote at my assigned polling place?
A: It depends on your county. Jackson County voters can vote at ANY of the 53 KC polling locations on Election Day. Clay County and Platte County voters must go to their assigned precinct location.

Q: Can I vote early?
A: Yes. Missouri allows no-excuse absentee voting. Early voting runs from March 24 through April 6, 2026 at the locations listed above.

Q: Where do I vote if I live in the Northland?
A: Northland residents may be in Jackson County, Clay County, or Platte County. Check your voter registration at https://voteroutreach.sos.mo.gov/portal/ to determine your county and polling place.

Q: I work in Kansas City but live elsewhere. Do I vote on this?
A: No. Only residents of Kansas City who are registered to vote within city limits can vote on the earnings tax renewal. However, the tax applies to your income earned in KC regardless of this vote's outcome until/unless voters choose not to renew it.

Q: What ID do I need to vote?
A: Missouri requires a valid photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, or other government-issued photo ID). If you don't have one, you can sign a sworn statement at the polls and still cast your ballot.

## Geographic Coverage

Kansas City, Missouri spans four counties. The earnings tax applies to all parts of Kansas City regardless of county:
- Jackson County: The largest portion of Kansas City. Includes downtown, midtown, the Country Club Plaza, Westport, Brookside, Waldo, and most of the city.
- Clay County: Includes the Northland neighborhoods of Gladstone, Liberty area, North Kansas City area, and Barry Road corridor.
- Platte County: Includes the KCI Airport area, Tiffany Springs, Platte Woods, Riverside, and Parkville-adjacent neighborhoods.
- Cass County: A very small portion of southern Kansas City. Very few KC residents live in this area.
